$comment: 🖱️ A wheel is applied at the point ITS OWN events carried, never at wherever the pointer has since moved. `🎮️wgpu-browser-input-wire/🔣️.json` already pins that a DOM wheel's position survives both hops into `DispatchEvent::Scroll { x, y, delta_x, delta_y }`; this oracle pins the hop AFTER it — what the frame does with that position. The wgpu tick is input-driven, so a wheel is normally drained by a LATER event, and the frame's scene-surface gate plus `World3dState::bounds.contains` both answer for whatever point it applies at.

rule.statement: Scroll events coalesce their deltas between frames; the newest scroll's own point is where the whole coalesced delta is applied. A pointer event moves the pointer and never the pending wheel's point. Taking the wheel leaves none, and a frame with no pending wheel applies nothing.

cases.name: one-notch-applies-at-its-own-point
cases.why: The baseline: a single wheel over the preview centre.

cases.name: a-later-pointer-move-does-not-move-the-pending-wheel
cases.why: The live defect, verbatim. The probe wheels over the preview centre and then nudges the pointer to the top-left corner to make the input-driven tick run. Measured on 6118 before the fix: `wheel gate x=5 y=5 delta=-480 hit=None control=None propagates=true worlds=[("procedural-preview", false)]` — four notches coalesced and applied 1200 px away from where the user scrolled, so the World3d authority saw `wheel=0` on every one of its 335 intents and the camera was byte-identical before and after (📓️wgpu-end-to-end-verification-2026-09-14.md §5.1).

cases.name: coalesced-notches-apply-at-the-newest-point
cases.why: A wheel stream that genuinely travels — trackpad momentum under a moving cursor. The newest event's point is where the whole coalesced delta lands, which is what a browser's own wheel stream means.

cases.name: taking-the-wheel-leaves-none
cases.why: A second frame with no new scroll applies nothing — the accumulator is not a level, it is a pending delta.

cases.name: opposite-notches-cancel-and-apply-nothing
cases.why: Zero delta is not a wheel. The frame must fall through without gating a surface or publishing a camera verb.

cases.name: pointer-events-alone-apply-nothing
cases.why: Moving the pointer must never invent a wheel.
